name: Non-syndromic Esophageal Malformation
aliases: Non-syndromic Esophageal Atresia and/or Tracheoesophageal Fistula

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnosis of Esophageal Atresia

criteria.description: Presence of esophageal discontinuity confirmed by inability to pass nasogastric tube into stomach
Identification of abnormal connection between trachea and esophagus by imaging or endoscopy
Chest and abdominal X-ray showing coiling of nasogastric tube in proximal esophageal pouch and gas patterns consistent with fistula
No associated anomalies or syndromic features identified on clinical and genetic evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of esophageal discontinuity confirmed by clinical and radiological findings without associated syndromic anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic forms.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inability to pass nasogastric tube beyond proximal esophagus
searchTerms: nasogastric tube blockage in upper esophagus
unable to pass feeding tube down throat

pathognomonic.symptomName: Excessive drooling and salivation in neonate
Cyanosis and choking during feeding due to aspiration
searchTerms: bluish skin and choking when feeding
food coming back up after feeding
failure to gain weight as baby

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible leukocytosis if pneumonia present
imaging: Chest and abdominal X-ray showing coiled nasogastric tube in proximal esophageal pouch
Contrast esophagogram demonstrating esophageal discontinuity and fistula
genetic: No specific genetic markers for non-syndromic forms; genetic testing used to exclude syndromic associations
other: Clinical observation of feeding difficulties and respiratory symptoms in neonate

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of additional congenital anomalies such as cardiac defects, limb abnormalities, or vertebral anomalies
Genetic syndromic markers or chromosomal abnormalities
Partial esophageal narrowing rather than complete discontinuity
Ability to pass nasogastric tube with resistance

redFlags: Inability to pass nasogastric tube into stomach
Severe respiratory distress or cyanosis during feeding
references: Lally KP, et al. Esophageal Atresia and Tracheoesophageal Fistula. In: Pediatric Surgery, 7th Edition. 2019.
Puri P, Höllwarth ME. Pediatric Surgery: Diagnosis and Management. 2018.
